name: Design-led
blurb: AI mocks up the screen first, plans from the approved mockup, builds it, then screenshots the real app next to the mockup for your review. No spec stage; you deploy by hand.

nodes.run:
Design card {ref}: make HTML mockups and upload them to the card. **Never write to the repo**: this worktree is shared. Work in `$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")`.

Each run is one round; a rejection sends the card back here with only the card as memory. Converge: get closer each round, and leave a trail.
1. **Read.** The description is the ask. Read the rejection note first, then every comment. Pull the current mockups: `{relay} mockups {ref} --pull "$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")/prev" --json`.
2. **Look at the real app**, if it runs: start it as `package.json` says, in the foreground under `timeout`, and only look. Build on what exists.
3. **Round 1: ask, usually instead of mocking.** Put every question in one needs-input: who it's for, what matters most on screen, empty and error states, mobile, what's fixed and what's your call. Don't ask what you can find out.
4. **Build** self-contained HTML: inline CSS, Google Fonts allowed, nothing else external. Reuse the app's look.
5. **Check** screenshots at desktop and phone width, and fix what's broken.
6. **Upload**: `{relay} mockups {ref} <a.html> <b.html> --caption "<decision A>" --caption "<decision B>"` (this replaces the list). Comment the round: what was asked, what changed, what you tried and dropped. Keep a short `## Design` list of decisions at the end of the description (`{relay} describe {ref} @<file>`), rewritten each round, never touching the text above it.
7. **Finish.** Several options → ask which wins. One direction → succeed; a human reviews it.

Rules: a rejection asking for a specific change → change only that. Options differ by a real decision, named in the caption. Rejected twice for the same reason → ask. Never succeed without a mockup.

Plan card {ref}: turn it into a short plan a human can approve and the Code flow can build. Write the plan, its tasks and its acceptance criteria to the card. Don't touch git; files you write go in `$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")`. Be brief: someone should be able to read the plan in a minute.

**Read** the card (`{relay} card {ref}`): the rejection note first, then the description and comments (earlier rounds and human answers). If the card has mockups, or its description names another card's, pull them: `{relay} mockups <ref> --pull "$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")/mockups" --json`. Many cards have none. Read enough of the repo to know where things go.
- Rejected after Code: tasks marked done have shipped, so leave them. Answer the note with new tasks, and update the plan and criteria where it changes them.
- Rejected at Plan review: revise the plan to answer the note; keep what it didn't mention.

**Ask** everything the description or Design left open (behaviour, edge cases, scope) in one needs-input batch, then stop. Don't ask what the repo or the mockups answer. If nothing is open, go straight to writing.

**Split** a card that needs more than 6 tasks or holds pieces that could ship separately. Propose it in the same batch: each new card's title and scope, plus "Keep it as one card". Only after it's approved: this card keeps the first slice. Create each other slice with `{relay} create "<title>" --stage Backlog --description @<file> --json`, add dependencies (`--depends-on`, or `{relay} depends <card> <blockers>`, which replaces the set), then `{relay} move <new ref> "Design:Done"`. Its description says what it covers and which of {ref}'s mockups apply ("Mockups: {ref}, <captions>"). Comment the new refs on {ref}.
A card depends on another only when the other makes something it uses, or when both would build the same new thing (pick one as the maker). Touching the same files isn't a dependency: blocked cards can't start, so leave those parallel.

**Plan** (`{relay} plan {ref} @<file>`): `## Goal` (one sentence), `## Approach` (2–4 bullets), `## Not doing`, `## Decisions` (what was settled, and whether it was answered or your call), `## Verification` (`Gate: npm test`).

**Tasks**: 1–6 in build order, each working and testable on its own. The implementer sees only its own task:
- **Build:** what to make, in a sentence or two, naming any file or function another task uses.
- **Tests:** one line per test, situation → expected result.
Remove tasks that aren't done (`{relay} tasks list {ref} --json`, then `{relay} task rm {ref} <id>`), then add the new ones in one call: `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "<title>" @<file> --task ...`.

**Acceptance criteria** (`{relay} criteria {ref} @<file>`): 2–5 checks a person could run:
### 1. <title>
1. <step>
2. Expect: <one thing you can see>
Describe what a user sees. Work with no UI gets commands instead ("`npm test` passes").

Write decisions, not code. Check with `{relay} tasks list {ref}`, then stop.

{relay} git-fetch && open=$(gh pr list --head {branch} --state open --json number -q length) && if [ "$open" -gt 0 ]; then base=origin/{branch}; else base=origin/main; fi && git checkout -B {branch} "$base" && { {relay} card {ref} --json --field plan | grep -q . || { echo 'card {ref} has no plan; send it back to Plan' >&2; exit 1; }; } && {relay} branch {ref} {branch}

Implement task {task_id} ("{task}"), and only this task.
1. Read it: `{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}`. Read the plan header: `{relay} card {ref} --json --field plan`.
2. Test first: for each Tests line, write the test, watch it fail, then make it pass.
3. Build only what the task asks, using the exact names it gives for anything other tasks use.
4. Run `npm test` and read the output.
5. Commit, with a message based on the task title.

Already built? Say so and run `{relay} outcome succeeded --no-changes`.
Report what changed and the test output.

Review task {task_id} ("{task}"), just committed, against its spec: `{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}`. Don't edit or commit. Read it with `git show` and `git diff`, and run `npm test`: a failing test is Critical.

Fail it only for Critical or Important problems:
- something the task asked for is missing, wrong, or untested (each Tests line needs a real test)
- something was built that it didn't ask for
- bugs, hard-to-follow code, or code that ignores the repo's conventions
Note minor polish, but pass.

If a FINDINGS block below holds your earlier findings, only check those were fixed; a new finding blocks only if it is Critical.
Decide first, then explain. Give each finding as `file:line`: problem → fix.

A review rejected task {task_id} ("{task}"); the findings are in the FINDINGS block below. Fix every one, staying inside this task (`{relay} task show {ref} {task_id}` if you need its spec). If a finding is wrong, say why.
Run `npm test`, then commit. Report each finding: fixed at `file:line`, or why not.

Review card {ref}'s whole branch for problems the per-task reviews couldn't see. Read-only.
- Spec: the plan header (`{relay} card {ref} --json --field plan`) and the tasks (`{relay} tasks list {ref}`).
- Diff: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`, then read it in slices by area.

Look for planned work that's missing or untested, tasks that clash (names, patterns, two solutions to one problem), broken callers, security or data-loss risks, and dead or unrequested code.
Only Critical or Important problems block; mention minor ones and pass. If tasks were already added from your last review, check those and block only on a new Critical problem.

To send work back: add it as tasks in one call, `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "<title>" @<file> [--task ...]`. Each body has **Build** (what to make), **Tests** (one line per test: situation → expected result) and your evidence. Then write why to `$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH` and run `{relay} outcome partial --detail @"$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH"`. `partial` returns the branch to implement.

Check card {ref} against its acceptance criteria: `{relay} card {ref} --json --field acceptance_criteria`. None? Pass.

Follow each criterion's steps literally and mark it **pass**, **fail** (say what happened instead) or **human-verify** (can't be checked here; say why). Never guess a pass.
If a step needs the app, start it as `package.json` says, in the foreground under `timeout`, and save screenshots to `$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")/acceptance/`. Don't edit code or commit.
Write the checklist, with screenshot paths, to `$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")/acceptance/report.md`; the results step posts it.

All pass or human-verify → succeeded. Any fail → send it back, quoting the criterion.
To send work back: add it as tasks in one call, `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "<title>" @<file> [--task ...]`. Each body has **Build** (what to make), **Tests** (one line per test: situation → expected result) and your evidence. Then write why to `$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH` and run `{relay} outcome partial --detail @"$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH"`. `partial` returns the branch to implement.
{relay} git-fetch && { git rebase origin/main || { git rebase --abort; exit 1; }; }

Rebasing onto origin/main hit conflicts (origin/main is fetched; the rebase was aborted). Run `git rebase origin/main` and resolve each conflict, keeping what both sides intended.
If a resolution needs a human, run `git rebase --abort` and ask. Never commit a guess. Report how you resolved each file.

`npm test` failed after rebasing card {ref} onto main; the output is in the message. Don't fix it; turn it into a task.
Find the cause, then add one task: `{relay} tasks add {ref} --task "Fix: <what>" @<file>`, with **Build** (what to fix), **Tests** (the failing tests by name) and the key output lines. Then declare succeeded; the flow goes back to implement.
If the cause is the environment (Node missing, network down), add nothing: declare failed and say why.

sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD); url=$(gh pr list --head {branch} --state merged --json url,headRefOid -q "map(select(.headRefOid == \"$sha\"))[0].url // empty"); if [ -n "$url" ]; then {relay} pr {ref} "$url"; exit 0; fi; if [ "$(git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD)" = 0 ]; then url=$(gh pr list --head {branch} --state merged --json url -q '.[0].url // empty'); if [ -n "$url" ]; then {relay} pr {ref} "$url"; exit 0; fi; echo 'nothing on {branch} beyond origin/main, and no merged PR for it' >&2; exit 1; fi; git push --force-with-lease origin HEAD:refs/heads/{branch} && url=$(gh pr list --head {branch} --state open --json url -q '.[0].url // empty') && { [ -n "$url" ] || url=$(gh pr create --fill --head {branch} --base main); } && {relay} pr {ref} "$url" && gh pr merge "$url" --squash --auto

Post card {ref}'s results.
1. Upload each screenshot listed in `$(dirname "$RELAY_NODE_SCRATCH")/acceptance/report.md`: `{relay} attach {ref} <path> --field url`.
2. Comment the checklist with those images: `{relay} comment {ref} @<file>`.
3. Record `{relay} result {ref} @<file>` in the shape relay.md gives. Write for a product owner: `summary` is 3–5 bullets on what to go look at; `changes` are short verb phrases ("Adds pantry search"); `screens` come from the uploads.
